question: Identify the root cause of the network fault: which device, what changed, and why it breaks.
description:
Mixed IOS-XR/IOS-XE fault: move R8's R8↔R6 link (Ethernet0/1) from
OSPF Area 3 to Area 4 on the IOS-XE (IOL) router R8; R6 (IOS-XR)
keeps its side (GigabitEthernet0/0/0/2) in Area 3. The two ends now
disagree on the area ID, each rejects the other's Hellos, and the
R6↔R8 adjacency drops — producing syslog in BOTH dialects: IOS-XE
%OSPF-* lines on R8 and IOS-XR %ROUTING-OSPF-* lines on R6.
expected_rca:
Root cause: on 100.64.0.108 (R8), interface Ethernet0/1 (the R8<->R6 link) was moved from OSPF area 3 into area 4, while R6 keeps its end of that link (GigabitEthernet0/0/0/2) in area 3.
The two ends now disagree on the area ID for the link; OSPF requires both neighbors on a link to share the same area ID, so each end rejects the other's Hellos, the R6<->R8 adjacency over Ethernet0/1 cannot form, and no routes are exchanged across that link.
Fix: return R8's Ethernet0/1 to OSPF area 3.
expected_symptoms_summary:
OSPF adjacency state change (%ROUTING-OSPF-5-ADJCHG):
- R6: neighbor 192.0.2.8 on GigabitEthernet0/0/0/2 (area 3) FULL → DOWN reason "dead timer expired".

OSPF adjacency state change (%OSPF-5-ADJCHG):
- R8: neighbor 192.0.2.6 on Ethernet0/1 FULL → DOWN reason "Interface down or detached".

apply.commands:
configure terminal
interface Ethernet0/1
ip ospf 100 area 4

revert.commands:
configure terminal
interface Ethernet0/1
ip ospf 100 area 3
